title: Android RD: display-selection UI + protocol wiring (primary default, pick display, both-screens)
description: Phone advertises SupportsDisplaySelection + SupportsTargetSwitch in DesktopConfig.ClientCapabilities, reads DesktopDisplayCatalog from the host, and adds a picker in the RD overlay: Primary (default) / each individual display / Both screens (VirtualDesktop combined wide frame). Live-switch mid-session via DesktopTargetSwitch; persist the choice in SettingsManager. Host validates targets already (RemoteDesktopHandler.TryApplyCaptureTarget / HandleTargetSwitchAsync).
notes: DISCOVERABILITY FIX (post-test): picker was only fetched at stream-start and could miss the 4s catalog-timeout fallback -> empty list -> no Display section even with 2 monitors. Added eager catalog pre-load on connect (RemoteDesktopViewModel.ensureDisplayCatalogLoaded() wired into isConnected collector; resets catalogRequested/displaysLoaded on disconnect) so the picker appears in settings without needing to stream first. Added Log.i diagnostics (tag RemoteDesktopVM): 'Requesting display catalog from host' + 'Display catalog received: N display(s), M option(s)'. Verified end-to-end: GetDesktopEndpoint() is connection-scoped (not stream-scoped); host EnumDisplayMonitors returns all monitors in Extend mode; proguard keeps RemexClientManager/RemexCallback {*;}. compileDebugKotlin OK.

title: Android RD: multi-monitor selection, zoom/pan, trackpad-follow, cursor fix, performance
description: Re-enable and finish two-monitor support on the Android remote-desktop client. Host-side display-selection infra (DesktopDisplayCatalog / DesktopCaptureTarget / DesktopTargetSwitch, VirtualDesktop+Monitor capture) is already built and unused by the phone. Default to primary monitor; let the user pick a single display or the combined (virtual-desktop) wide frame. Also improve zoom/pan, add trackpad follow-cursor auto-pan, fix the dual-cursor artifact in the combined view, and raise streaming performance. Scope: Android only (host done). Desktop client is a possible later follow-up.

title: 100% localization across both the Android and AvaloniaUI apps
description: Identify all hardcoded strings in Android and AvaloniaUI and extract/translate them, and ensure all existing strings are translated.
close_reason: Completed extraction, translation, and build validation of all 100% localized resources across Android and Avalonia UI apps, resolving AAPT2 escape errors and Kotlin compilation issues.

title: Android RD: streaming performance (~35fps cap) — H.264 default, fps, pipeline profiling
description: Effective fps caps ~35 because default codec is MJPEG (full-frame CPU JPEG every frame). Confirm/default H.264 (FFmpeg) negotiation end-to-end on Android, raise default targetFps, and profile capture->encode->send using existing handler metrics (avgCaptureMs/avgSendMs/captured-vs-sent). Goal: materially higher fps on capable PC+phone.
notes:
ROOT CAUSE (from user RTX 5080 + 2x 2560x1440 combined = 5120x1440 @ ~100% scale, fps=120): NVENC H.264 rejected params because H.264 NVENC is hard-capped at 4096x4096 on EVERY NVIDIA GPU (codec limit, not generational). 5120>4096 -> nvenc fails to open -> stream silently fell back to MJPEG (~35fps). Two compounding bugs.

FIX 1 (FFmpegH264Encoder.TryStartFFmpeg): false-success detection. The 150ms liveness window passed before nvenc failed-to-open (~a few hundred ms in), so it reported success and the codec-fallback loop (qsv/amf/libx264) never ran. Widened window 150ms->900ms; a healthy rawvideo-pipe encoder never self-exits, so an exit in-window = unambiguous failure. Now logs the real ffmpeg error at Warning and falls through.

FIX 2 (RemoteDesktopHandler): cap H.264 encode surface to 4096 (MaxH264EncodeDimension). New ClampScaleForH264() + _h264CaptureScale field; TryCreateH264Encoder downscales just enough to fit and STORES the scale; the H.264 capture call (CaptureRawScreenAsync) now uses _h264CaptureScale so capture size == encoder -s WxH (self-heal at line ~337 still guards drift). For 5120x1440 -> 4096x1152 -> NVENC opens; 120fps trivial for the 5080. Single-monitor (<=4096) unchanged/full-res.

Compiles: Host build OK, host tests 207/207. HOST-SIDE change -> user must rebuild/restart Remex.Host (not the Android app). Pending verification: combined view should now stream hardware H.264 (h264_nvenc) at high fps instead of MJPEG. Possible follow-up: meta PixelWidth still reports full (unscaled) width; H.264 SPS drives the Android decoder so OK, but could report actual encoded dims for correctness.

title: Android RD: dual cursor in combined virtual-desktop view (baked real cursor + Android overlay)
description: In VirtualDesktop capture the host bakes the real Windows cursor (DxgiDesktopCapture.DrawCursorOnBitmap, virtual-desktop origin) AND streams DesktopCursorState for the Android overlay, so one monitor shows the real cursor and the other the Android-drawn one. Coordinate-origin mismatch. Fix: when client SupportsCursorState, suppress host baking and draw a single Android overlay cursor using virtual-desktop coordinates.
notes: EDGE-CASE FIX IMPLEMENTED (compiles: Host build OK, compileDebugKotlin OK, host tests 207/207). Added DesktopMeta.CursorVisible (bool, default true for legacy compat). Host RemoteDesktopHandler: new IsCursorInRegion() helper; set CursorVisible on both the per-update meta (SendCursorUpdateAsync) and bootstrap meta (SendCurrentStreamBootstrapAsync) = cursor within [desktopLeft,desktopLeft+screenWidth) x [desktopTop,...). Android VM meta parser: when cursorVisible==false, set _hostCursorX/Y=-1f (hide); screen mapHostToLocal already returns null for <0 coords (also fixes pre-first-report corner-cursor glitch). Net: in single-Monitor capture the overlay hides when the pointer is on another display instead of clamping to the edge; VirtualDesktop = always in-region = always shown. Primary dual-cursor cause (host baking) already handled by drawCursor=false. Needs native rebuild (DesktopMeta is in Remex.Core->libRemexCore.so). Pending user verification of Both-screens single-cursor + off-region hide.

title: Android RD: improve zoom/pan UX (clamping, edge scroll, focal pinch-zoom)
description: Make panning to the far left/right easy and bound zoom sensibly to the frame pixel size. Fix pinch-zoom focal point, min/max clamps, and edge-scroll so the combined wide frame is comfortable to navigate. In RemoteDesktopScreen.kt (Offset/IntOffset transform state).

title: Android RD: trackpad-mode follow-cursor auto-pan when zoomed
description: In relative/trackpad mouse mode while zoomed in, auto-pan the viewport so the cursor never leaves the visible area (Windows-App side-scroll behavior). The zoomed image side-scrolls to keep the cursor on screen. Depends on the zoom/pan rework.
